newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Countries outside EMU will suffer - EU Commissioner.
newsitem.headline: Countries outside EMU will suffer - EU Commissioner.

text.p: Countries which will stay outside the European Union's planned economic and monetary union will suffer economically, EU Industrial Affairs Commissioner Martin Bangemann said on Wednesday.
"I personally believe that those who stay out will suffer from that," he told a press conference.
Bangemann said there would be no sudden exodus from for example London as a place to raise funds if Britain decided to stay out when monetary union is introduced in 1999.
But, the German commissioner added, "you will have a creeping effect which is negative."
For example, investors seeking security would feel safer in the euro-zone and the cost of capital would be lower.
"So there are all kinds of difficulties," Bangemann added.
If Britain decides to stay outside, the domestic debate would change in substance and tone, he said. "Those who are suffering from being out will start a debate (on) why shouldn't we now join."
Bangemann stressed that the Commission did not want to put pressure on any country to join EMU.
